explanation: The I84V mutation reduces lopinavir binding by eliminating a critical hydrophobic contact in the S1/S1' subpocket. Isoleucine's larger branched side chain at position 84 (2.4 Å from the ligand) provides favorable van der Waals interactions with lopinavir's nonpolar moieties, while the smaller, less bulky valine side chain leaves a cavity that weakens this hydrophobic packing interaction. This loss of optimal shape complementarity and van der Waals surface contact, despite the substitution remaining within the nonpolar character class, destabilizes the inhibitor-protein complex sufficiently to confer resistance.
